extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination of U.S. patent applications including use of Patentability Reports, determining patentability under 35 U.S.C. §§101/102/103, choice of prior art, effective filing date rules, and procedures for rejecting and overcoming rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of examination for Patentability Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: When supervisory patent examiners in a P.R. case cannot agree as to the order of examination by their Technology Centers (TCs), the supervisory patent examiner having jurisdiction will direct that a complete search be made of the art relevant to his or her claims prior to referring the application to another TC for report. The TC to which the application is referred will be advised of the results of this search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supervisory examiners think a different sequence of search is expedient, the order of search should be correspondingly modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and recording Patentability Reports (P.R.s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forwarding an application for a Patentability Report is not treated as a transfer by the forwarding TC; when the P.R. is completed and the application is returned to the forwarding TC, it is not counted as a receipt or action by transfer, though credit is given for the time spent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date status in the reporting TC is determined based on dates in the TC of original jurisdiction. A timely reminder should be furnished to the TC making the P.R. to ensure orderly progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate prints of drawings for P.R. applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In P.R. applications having drawings, the assigned examiner will furnish to the TC to which the application is referred prints of the applicable drawing sheets for interference search purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate that prints were furnished (e.g., pencil notation). When application is allowed or abandoned, notify each TC that submitted a P.R.; reporting TC should note date of allowance/abandonment on duplicate prints and may destroy prints when of no value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on use of Patentability Report practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability Report practice is discretionary and should be used only where it will save total examiner time or improve quality due to specialized knowledge. It is never proper where claims are directed to the same character of invention but differ in scope only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where P.R. is ordinarily not proper include (A) product/process manufacturing pairs, (B) product and process that merely makes the product, and (C) combinations distinguished solely by a subcombination. A P.R. may be used when it demonstrably saves examiner time with Director of Technology Center approval (mark 'Approved' on request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews with applicants in P.R. cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When an interview is held on an application in which a Patentability Report has been adopted, the reporting TC may be called on for assistance at the interview concerning claims treated by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§713–713.10 regarding interview procedures in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline claim examination goals
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the application, performing a prior art search, and analyzing application against the prior art, the examiner should determine whether the claims define a useful, novel, nonobvious, and enabled invention clearly described in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal of examination is to clearly articulate any rejection early so the applicant can respond; examiner should review all evidence, arguments, and responses before issuing the next Office action. Require information reasonably necessary under 37 CFR 1.105 generally prior to or with the first Office action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to cite best references and explain pertinence
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejecting claims for want of novelty or obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. For complex references or references showing multiple inventions, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pertinence is not apparent, it must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible reliance on admissions and facts of record
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant, or patent owner in reexamination, and may rely upon facts within his or her knowledge as permitted by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject matter developed by another that is prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g) may be used under 35 U.S.C. 103 unless the entire rights were commonly owned or subject to obligation of assignment at the time the claimed invention was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims precluded by statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an original application naming an inventor will be rejected as precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed in both the application and the statutory invention registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar rejection rules apply to reissue applications seeking subject matter waived in statutory invention registrations; criteria (i) and (ii) in regulation specify when preclusion applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of patentability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of patentability (novelty, usefulness, unobviousness under 35 U.S.C. §§101, 102, 103) must be the same throughout the Office; all requirements must be met before a claim is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim should not be allowed merely because it recites all features ('picture' claim). Applications should not be allowed unless patentability issues have been raised and resolved. Apply 'preponderance of the evidence' test: reject if more likely than not unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive handling of defects in form or omission of limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: When patentable subject matter is disclosed but claims cannot be allowed due to defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's action should be constructive and, when possible, offer a definite suggestion for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting patentable disclosed but not claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is satisfied that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and the record indicates the applicant intends to claim it, the Office action may note that certain aspects/features have not been claimed and that if properly claimed such claims may be given favorable consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after applicant's reply (37 CFR 1.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a reply by applicant to a non-final action, the application will be reconsidered and again examined; applicant will be notified if claims are rejected, objections made, or decisions favorable to patentability are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may reply in the same manner as after the first examination unless action is made final, an appeal has been taken, prosecution is closed, or a right of appeal notice has been mailed. Once an appeal is taken, amendments are subject to appeal provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between 'rejection' and 'objection'
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal to grant claims because subject matter is unpatentable is a 'rejection'; improper claim form matters are 'objections'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections (merits) are reviewable by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences; objections (formal matters) are generally reviewable only by petition to the Commissioner and should not be combined in appeals to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection on prior art (35 U.S.C. 102 and 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most frequent grounds of rejection are lack of novelty under 35 U.S.C. 102 or obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103. Language used in rejecting claims should be unequivocal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §707.07(d) for guidance on phrasing rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of prior art; use the best available art
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art rejections should ordinarily be confined strictly to the best available art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions permitted where (A) propriety of rejection depends on particular claim interpretation, (B) claim met only in terms by a reference that does not disclose inventive concept, or (C) most pertinent reference likely to be antedated by a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration. Avoid merely cumulative rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 102, the reference must teach every aspect of the claimed invention explicitly or implicitly (anticipation). Under 35 U.S.C. 103, the reference teachings must be modified in a way that would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§2131–2146 for detailed guidance on determinations under 102 and 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining the effective filing date of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective filing date rules: (A) continuation/divisional with 35 U.S.C. 120 satisfied → effective date same as earliest filing date in line; (B) continuation-in-part → claims not supported by parent get new filing date, supported claims get parent's date; (C) foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) → effective filing date is U.S. filing date unless (A) or (B) applies; (D) 35 U.S.C. 119(e) provisional priority → effective filing date is provisional filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP §§706.02(b), 2136.05, 1893.03(b), 201.11(a), 1895 for related situations and PCT national stage issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining whether to apply 35 U.S.C. 102(a), (b), or (e)
rubrics_metrics.description: After finding a printed publication or patent disclosing the claimed invention, determine which subsection of 35 U.S.C. 102 applies by comparing the effective filing date of the application with the date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider 102(b) first (statutory bar if reference >1 year before effective filing date). If 102(b) does not apply because reference is too recent, consider 102(e) and then 102(a) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining reference issue or publication date
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish the issue or publication date of the reference so proper date comparison can be made (e.g., a magazine is effective as of the date it reached the addressee, not the mailing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreign patents and other specific situations consult relevant MPEP sections and case law (e.g., MPEP §707.05(f), §2124, §2126, §§2128–2128.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-PG-PUB vs PG-PUB classification for applying 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 or filed prior and voluntarily published are 'PG-PUB' and are subject to the current 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (including U.S. patents, U.S. application publications, certain international application publications as prior art). Applications filed prior to Nov 29, 2000 and not voluntarily published are 'pre PG-PUB' and are subject to the former version of 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (limited to U.S. patents filed earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examining PG-PUB applications, references can include U.S. patents, U.S. application publications, and certain international publications (with conditions). For pre PG-PUB, the reference must be a U.S. patent (or SIR) with earlier filing date and the inventive entity must be different from that of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for 35 U.S.C. 102(e) to apply (PG-PUB and pre PG-PUB)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre PG-PUB: reference must be a U.S. patent (or SIR) with filing date earlier than effective filing date, and inventive entity must be different. For PG-PUB: reference may be a U.S. patent, U.S. application publication, or qualifying international application publication with filing date earlier than the application and inventive entity must be different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply for patents/applications entitled to benefit of provisional filing dates under 35 U.S.C. 119(e). International applications are prior art under 102(e) only under specified conditions (e.g., published in English under PCT Article 21(2)(a) and designated the U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(b) can be overcome by: (A) arguing the claims are patentably distinguishable; (B) amending the claims to be patentably distinguishable; (C) perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 by amending specification or filing an application data sheet referencing the prior application; (D) filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration showing prior invention (where appropriate); (E) perfecting foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) with certified priority documents; (F) perfecting priority under 119(e) or 120 via specification amendment or ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference and the application claim the same invention or obvious variants, a 1.131 affidavit is not acceptable; consider double patenting or interference as appropriate (see MPEP §804 and Chapter 2300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(e) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections based on 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(e) can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentable distinctness over the prior art; (B) amending the claims to patentably distinguish over the prior art; (C) filing affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (for (e)) or 1.132/1.131 (for (a)) where appropriate to show prior invention or that the reference invention is not by 'another'; (D) perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), 119(e) or 120 where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 102(e) specifically, a 1.132 declaration may show the reference invention is not by 'another'; see MPEP §§715, 715.01(a), 715.01(c), and 716.10 for affidavit/declaration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections based on knowledge by others, public use, or sale (35 U.S.C. 102(a)/(b) topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) may be based on public use, knowledge by others, or on-sale conditions as statutory bars to patentability under the applicable subsection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Text continues in MPEP §706.02(c) for specific guidance and factual inquiries required to determine whether such activities constitute prior art or statutory bars.)
